newsitem.title: INDIA: India orders probe into bank losses.
newsitem.headline: India orders probe into bank losses.

text.p: The Indian government has ordered an investigation into the loss of 13.36 billion rupees ($374 million) by the state-owned Indian Bank in 1995/96 (April-March), the Press Trust of India reported on Friday.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said that the Reserve Bank of India and the banking department have been asked by the government to investigate the bank's affairs.
Several legislators have expressed concern about state-owned banks being saddled with huge non-performing loans. These are loans that borrowers are having difficulty repaying.
Chidambaram said that in 1995/96 the banks recovered 40.05 billion rupees of non-performing assets against 41.97 billion in the previous year.
The Indian Bank reported the losses in July. It has not issued any statement explaining the losses. ($1 = 35.75 rupees)
